items.title: Lutetium-177 PSMA Therapy for Oligometastatic Prostate Cancer After Definitive Treatment
items.summary: This phase 3 trial tests whether Pluvicto (lutetium-177 PSMA therapy) can help men with limited metastatic prostate cancer that has returned after initial treatment. The study compares treatment with Pluvicto versus observation (monitoring without immediate treatment). The goal is to control cancer recurrence and delay the need for hormone therapy while preserving quality of life.

items.title: Actinium-225 PSMA Plus Hormone Therapy for Metastatic Castration-Resistant Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This phase 3 trial tests a new radioactive treatment (actinium-225 PSMA) combined with hormone therapy versus standard treatments for metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer. Patients must have progressed on one hormone therapy but not yet received chemotherapy or previous PSMA radioligand therapy. The study measures how long before cancer progresses on scans.

items.title: Luxdegalutamide Plus Abiraterone for Metastatic Hormone-Sensitive Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This phase 2 trial tests a new hormone therapy drug (luxdegalutamide) combined with abiraterone in men with metastatic hormone-sensitive prostate cancer. The study compares different doses of the combination against standard hormone therapy to determine the best dose and whether it works better than current treatments.

items.title: Adding Docetaxel to Hormone Therapy for Metastatic Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This phase 3 trial examines whether adding chemotherapy (docetaxel) to hormone therapy helps patients with metastatic hormone-sensitive prostate cancer who have suboptimal PSA response to initial hormone treatment. The study compares standard hormone therapy alone versus adding docetaxel to see if the combination better controls cancer growth and spread.

items.title: Mevrometostat Plus Enzalutamide for Metastatic Castration-Sensitive Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This phase 3 trial tests whether combining an investigational drug (mevrometostat) with enzalutamide works better than enzalutamide alone in patients with metastatic castration-sensitive prostate cancer who have not yet received hormone therapy or chemotherapy. The study aims to delay cancer progression.

items.title: Pocenbrodib Alone or With Darolutamide for Metastatic Castration-Resistant Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This early-phase trial tests the safety and anticancer activity of pocenbrodib, a new drug, either alone or combined with darolutamide in patients with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer. The study will determine safe doses and gather preliminary evidence of whether the drug combinations are effective.

items.title: Multiple Radioligand Therapies for Neuroendocrine Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This phase 1 trial evaluates different radioactive treatments targeting three different proteins (PSMA, SSTR2, and GRPR) on cancer cells in men with metastatic neuroendocrine prostate cancer. The study uses imaging to identify which target is most present on each patient's tumor, then treats with the corresponding radioligand therapy.

items.title: Bipolar Androgen Therapy to Restore Treatment Sensitivity in Metastatic CRPC
items.summary: This phase 1 trial tests whether cycling testosterone levels between very low and very high (bipolar androgen therapy) can restore sensitivity to hormone therapy in men with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer. The approach aims to suppress cancer growth, reduce PSA levels, and potentially delay disease progression.

items.title: Luxdegalutamide Plus Lutetium-177 PSMA for Metastatic Castration-Resistant Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This phase 2 trial evaluates combining a new hormone therapy (luxdegalutamide) with Pluvicto (lutetium-177 PSMA) in metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer patients previously treated with at least one hormone therapy and up to two chemotherapy regimens. The study compares different doses of the combination versus Pluvicto alone.

items.title: Tulmimetostat Combinations for Metastatic Hormone-Sensitive Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This phase 1/2 trial tests the safety and effectiveness of combining tulmimetostat (an investigational drug) with either darolutamide or abiraterone in men with newly diagnosed or recurrent metastatic hormone-sensitive prostate cancer. The study will evaluate how well tolerated the combinations are and whether they control cancer growth.

items.title: HER2-Targeted Therapy Plus Enzalutamide for Metastatic Castration-Resistant Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This phase 2 trial tested whether combining two HER2-targeted antibodies (pertuzumab and trastuzumab) with enzalutamide works in men with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer. The study has completed enrollment and results will show whether targeting HER2, a protein sometimes found on prostate cancer cells, provides benefit.

items.title: Opevesostat Versus Standard Hormone Therapy for Metastatic Castration-Resistant Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This phase 3 trial compares opevesostat, a novel drug targeting a specific enzyme, with standard hormone therapy (abiraterone or enzalutamide) in metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer patients who progressed on one prior hormone therapy. The study tests whether opevesostat can delay cancer progression better than switching to another hormone therapy.

items.title: Actinium-225 PSMA Plus Olaparib for Metastatic Castration-Resistant Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This phase 2 trial tests combining FPI-2265 (an actinium-225 radioactive treatment targeting PSMA) with olaparib (a PARP inhibitor) in men with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer. The study evaluates safety, tolerability, and whether this combination can effectively treat advanced disease. Enrollment is complete and the study is actively following participants.

items.title: Cabozantinib Plus Lutetium-177 PSMA Dose-Finding Study for Metastatic CRPC
items.summary: This phase 1 trial tests different doses of cabozantinib (a targeted therapy drug) combined with Pluvicto (lutetium-177 PSMA) in men with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer. The study aims to identify safe and effective doses of this combination. Currently suspended but may resume.

items.title: Radium-223 Versus Hormone Therapy for Bone Metastatic Castration-Resistant Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This phase 4 trial compares radium-223 (Xofigo), a radioactive treatment targeting bone metastases, with standard hormone therapy (abiraterone or enzalutamide) in men with castration-resistant prostate cancer that has spread to bone and progressed on one prior hormone therapy. The study evaluates effectiveness and safety of both approaches.

items.title: Lutetium-177 PSMA Plus Standard Treatment for Metastatic Hormone-Sensitive Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This large phase 3 international trial tests whether adding Pluvicto (lutetium-177 PSMA) to standard hormone therapy improves outcomes compared to standard hormone therapy alone in men with metastatic hormone-sensitive prostate cancer. Over 1,100 patients enrolled across 20 countries. The study evaluates whether earlier use of PSMA therapy benefits patients.

items.title: Niraparib Combination Therapies for Metastatic Castration-Resistant Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This phase 2 trial tests different combinations of niraparib (a PARP inhibitor) with other drugs in men with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer. The study determines safe doses and evaluates whether niraparib combinations show anticancer activity. Enrollment is complete and the study is actively following participants.

items.title: Blocking EGFR Pathway Overcomes Resistance to Enzalutamide in AR-V7 Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This research discovered that prostate cancer cells with AR splice variants develop resistance to enzalutamide by increasing EGFR protein levels and activating growth pathways. The study identified a feedback loop involving ELF1, EGFR, and ERK that drives tumor growth. Blocking EGFR or ERK may overcome resistance in patients whose cancer expresses AR variants.

items.title: Real-World Results of Lutetium-177 PSMA Therapy in Brazilian Patients
items.summary: This Brazilian study analyzed outcomes from 43 heavily pre-treated metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer patients who received lutetium-177 PSMA therapy. About 40% had a significant PSA decline of 50% or more. The study found that patients with visceral disease had poorer outcomes, consistent with other research showing that liver or lung metastases respond less well to PSMA therapy.

items.title: Comparing Hormone Therapy Versus Docetaxel as First Treatment for Metastatic Disease
items.summary: This real-world study compared hormone therapy drugs (ARPIs like abiraterone and enzalutamide) with chemotherapy (docetaxel) as first-line treatment in 148 metastatic hormone-sensitive prostate cancer patients. Hormone therapy provided longer time before disease progression on scans (69 versus 19 months) while overall survival was similar between groups. This suggests hormone therapy may be preferred as initial treatment.

items.title: Targeted Radiation After Hormone Therapy for Limited Metastatic Disease Study
items.source: European journal of nuclear medicine and molecular imaging
items.summary: This phase 2 trial tested a response-adapted approach where patients with limited metastatic hormone-sensitive prostate cancer received three cycles of apalutamide, then had PSMA PET scans. Patients with 10 or fewer visible metastases on the scan received additional targeted therapy including surgery or radiation to remaining disease sites to potentially improve cure rates.

items.title: CDK4/6 Inhibitor Enhances Enzalutamide Effectiveness in Preclinical Prostate Cancer Models
items.summary: This laboratory study found that combining dalpiciclib (a CDK4/6 inhibitor) with enzalutamide showed strong antitumor activity in castration-resistant prostate cancer cell and animal models. The combination worked by blocking DNA replication through a protein called MCM4. This research suggests CDK4/6 inhibitors might help overcome resistance to enzalutamide.

items.title: Real-World Comparison of Enzalutamide and Apalutamide in Japanese Patients
items.summary: This Japanese study compared enzalutamide and apalutamide in 227 metastatic hormone-sensitive prostate cancer patients using statistical matching to account for baseline differences. Both drugs showed similar effectiveness in terms of PSA response, time to castration resistance, and overall survival, with over 90% of patients achieving major PSA declines on both treatments.

items.title: Dual BRD4/AKT Inhibitor Overcomes c-MYC Resistance in Advanced Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This research developed a new dual-target drug (compound 21d) that blocks both BRD4 and AKT proteins in metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer. The drug addresses a common resistance mechanism where cancer cells increase c-MYC protein levels to escape treatment. Laboratory studies showed this dual inhibitor effectively suppressed cancer growth by targeting both pathways simultaneously.

items.title: Deeper PSA Decline Predicts Better Outcomes in Non-Metastatic CRPC
items.summary: This study of 349 non-metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer patients found that achieving greater than 96% PSA decline (beyond the standard 90% benchmark) with hormone therapy was associated with significantly longer progression-free survival. Men with very deep PSA responses had 78% lower risk of progression compared to those with less than 90% decline.

items.title: AR-V7 Splice Variant Mechanisms and Treatment Strategies Review
items.summary: This comprehensive review explains how AR-V7, a modified androgen receptor protein lacking the drug-binding region, drives resistance to hormone therapies in castration-resistant prostate cancer. The article describes how AR-V7 functions continuously without needing hormones, discusses the proteins that regulate its production and stability, and reviews potential therapeutic strategies to target AR-V7.

items.title: DDX3X Protein Regulates Androgen Receptor Through RNA G-Quadruplex Structures
items.summary: This research discovered how DDX3X, an RNA-binding protein, regulates androgen receptor production in androgen receptor-low/negative castration-resistant prostate cancer that develops after hormone therapy. DDX3X recognizes specific folded RNA structures (G-quadruplexes) in androgen receptor messenger RNA, controlling its translation into protein. This mechanism may explain some cases of treatment resistance.

items.title: Single Scan Dosimetry Predicts Response and Toxicity of Lutetium-177 PSMA
items.source: European journal of nuclear medicine and molecular imaging
items.summary: This study of 59 metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer patients found that bone marrow radiation dose from a single scan after the first Pluvicto treatment predicted blood cell toxicity. Higher doses to bone marrow correlated with decreased red blood cells. The research suggests that dosimetry (measuring radiation doses to organs) after just one treatment can help predict side effects.

items.title: Meta-Analysis of Immune Checkpoint Inhibitors in Metastatic Castration-Resistant Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This analysis of 1,580 patients from 21 clinical trials found that immune checkpoint inhibitors showed modest activity in unselected metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer patients. One-year overall survival was 63% and one-year progression-free survival was 17%. Combination therapies with immunotherapy plus other agents showed more benefit than immunotherapy alone, suggesting combinations may be more promising.
